container_info.reasoning: The project is to create documentation (static document site) and the container already includes MkDocs and Sphinx along with Python and Node toolchains. MkDocs is a lightweight, headless-friendly static documentation generator written in Python that is well suited for producing the requested document structure and works easily in a container. Platform is 'utility' because this is a documentation/build utility rather than a web application or backend service.
requirements: python3 (already present) and python3-pip for installing/using MkDocs
mkdocs (installed) and mkdocs-material theme (pip install mkdocs-material) — theme optional but common
git for source control and to fetch themes/templates (already present)
a minimal mkdocs.yml configuration file describing site_name and nav structure matching the document outline
documentation source files in Markdown under docs/ (index.md and pages matching outline)
npm/node only if using additional frontend tooling or custom themes (optional; present if needed)
headless build command: mkdocs build --clean to generate site into site/ (no server needed for static output)
lightweight local preview (optional) using mkdocs serve only for development (bind to 0.0.0.0 in container if needed)
minimal testing: a simple script to verify generated HTML exists (e.g., check for site/index.html) rather than a full test suite
environment: ensure $LANG and locale are set appropriately for deterministic builds; no production services required

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Persist deterministic locale and authoritative workspace variable via /etc/profile.d, ensure python3, python3 -m pip, git, and curl availability. Writes /etc/profile.d/mkdocs_env.sh and /etc/profile.d/mkdocs_workspace.sh idempotently using sudo; sources workspace env for the current run. Non-fatal warning if /etc/profile.d not writable. Operates in workspace: /tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-draft-236747-236748/Documentation.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# authoritative workspace provided by orchestration; fallback to container info path
: "${WORKSPACE:-/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-draft-236747-236748/Documentation}"
WS="${WORKSPACE}"
mkdir -p "$WS" && mkdir -p "$WS/tools/logs"
# Persist locale and workspace env via /etc/profile.d (idempotent)
PROF_ENV=/etc/profile.d/mkdocs_env.sh
PROF_WS=/etc/profile.d/mkdocs_workspace.sh
TMP_ENV=$(mktemp)
cat >"$TMP_ENV" <<'EOF'
export LANG=C.UTF-8
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
EOF
TMP_WS=$(mktemp)
cat >"$TMP_WS" <<EOF
export WORKSPACE="$WS"
export PATH="$PATH"
EOF
# write files using sudo if possible
if sudo --non-interactive true 2>/dev/null; then
  sudo sh -c 'cmp -s "$TMP_ENV" "$PROF_ENV" 2>/dev/null || cp "$TMP_ENV" "$PROF_ENV" && chmod 644 "$PROF_ENV"'
  sudo sh -c 'cmp -s "$TMP_WS" "$PROF_WS" 2>/dev/null || cp "$TMP_WS" "$PROF_WS" && chmod 644 "$PROF_WS"'
else
  echo "warning: cannot write /etc/profile.d (sudo unavailable); workspace env will be exported for this shell only" >&2
fi
rm -f "$TMP_ENV" "$TMP_WS"
# Make effective for current run
export LANG=C.UTF-8
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
export WORKSPACE="$WS"
# Verify required tools
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo "python3 missing" >&2; exit 2; }
python3 --version >/dev/null
python3 -m pip --version >/dev/null || (sudo apt-get update -q >/dev/null && sudo apt-get install -y -q python3-pip >/dev/null)
command -v git >/dev/null || { echo "git missing" >&2; exit 3; }
command -v curl >/dev/null || { echo "curl missing" >&2; exit 4; }
# mkdocs should be available per image; report if not importable but do not hard-fail
if python3 -c "import mkdocs" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c "import mkdocs; print('mkdocs', mkdocs.__version__)"
else
  echo "warning: mkdocs not importable by python3; subsequent steps may attempt to install theme but mkdocs must be available" >&2
fi

steps.name: install-theme-dependency
steps.description: Install mkdocs-material into the same python3 interpreter used by mkdocs if not present. Performs an executed compatibility check between installed mkdocs and mkdocs-material; allows optional PKG_VER pin via environment. Logs go to workspace/tools/logs. Operates in workspace: /tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-draft-236747-236748/Documentation.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# use authoritative workspace from env
: "${WORKSPACE:?workspace must be set by env-001}"
WS="${WORKSPACE}"
cd "$WS"
PY=python3
PIP="$PY -m pip"
PKG_NAME="mkdocs-material"
PKG_VER="${PKG_VER:-}" # optionally set by caller, e.g. PKG_VER==9.1.10
PKG_SPEC="$PKG_NAME${PKG_VER}"
LOG_DIR="$WS/tools/logs"; mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
INSTALL_LOG="$LOG_DIR/mkdocs-material-install.log"
# read mkdocs version (if present)
MKDOCS_VER=$($PY -c "import mkdocs,sys; print(mkdocs.__version__)" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
if [ -z "$MKDOCS_VER" ]; then
  echo "warning: mkdocs not found in python3; attempting to install mkdocs-material may fail" >&2
fi
# If already importable, skip install
if $PY -c "import importlib; importlib.import_module('mkdocs_material')" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  $PY -c "import mkdocs, mkdocs_material; print('mkdocs', getattr(mkdocs,'__version__','none'),'mkdocs_material',getattr(mkdocs_material,'__version__','unknown'))"
  exit 0
fi
# attempt install
$PIP install --disable-pip-version-check --no-input $PKG_SPEC >"$INSTALL_LOG" 2>&1 || { echo "mkdocs-material install failed; see $INSTALL_LOG" >&2; tail -n 200 "$INSTALL_LOG" >&2 || true; exit 3; }
# post-install compatibility check: run a small python snippet
$PY - <<'PY'
import sys
try:
    import mkdocs
    import mkdocs_material
except Exception as e:
    print('import-failed', e, file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(4)
mv = getattr(mkdocs, '__version__', '')
mmv = getattr(mkdocs_material, '__version__', '')
# basic compatibility heuristic: if mkdocs major version < 1 and mkdocs_material >=9 then warn
try:
    mja = int(mv.split('.')[0]) if mv else 0
except:
    mja = 0
print('mkdocs', mv, 'mkdocs_material', mmv)
if mja and mja < 1:
    print('warning: mkdocs major version <1; verify mkdocs-material compatibility', file=sys.stderr)
PY

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Build the site, start mkdocs serve in a controlled process (exec'd so PID maps to python server), poll localhost until responsive (configurable VALIDATION_TIMEOUT), capture logs to workspace/tools/logs/serve.log, then stop server cleanly by killing the PID or process group and waiting. Provides evidence that the environment and server work. Operates in workspace: /tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-draft-236747-236748/Documentation.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${WORKSPACE:?}"
WS="${WORKSPACE}"
cd "$WS"
TOOLS="$WS/tools"
LOG_DIR="$WS/tools/logs"; mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
SERVE_LOG="$LOG_DIR/serve.log"
: >"$SERVE_LOG"
command -v curl >/dev/null || (echo "curl missing" >&2; exit 2)
# build via helper and capture log
if ! "$TOOLS/build.sh" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/build.log"; then
  echo "build failed; see $LOG_DIR/build.log" >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOG_DIR/build.log" >&2 || true; exit 6
fi
[ -f "$WS/site/index.html" ] || (echo "site/index.html missing" >&2; exit 6)
# start server in its own process group so we can reliably kill it
# prefer executing the helper directly (it uses exec), so $! is the mkdocs python PID
nohup "$TOOLS/start.sh" >"$SERVE_LOG" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!
# give a moment for process group to settle
sleep 0.5
# determine PGID; if setsid used or exec'd, PGID should equal SERVER_PID
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo "")
TIMEOUT=${VALIDATION_TIMEOUT:-30}
elapsed=0
while [ $elapsed -lt $TIMEOUT ]; do
  if curl -sS --fail http://127.0.0.1:8000/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
  elapsed=$((elapsed+1))
done
if [ $elapsed -ge $TIMEOUT ]; then
  echo "server did not respond within ${TIMEOUT}s" >&2
  tail -n 400 "$SERVE_LOG" >&2 || true
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then
    kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    sleep 1
    kill -KILL -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  else
    kill "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  exit 7
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${WORKSPACE:?}"
WS="${WORKSPACE}"
cd "$WS"
TOOLS="$WS/tools"
LOG_DIR="$WS/tools/logs"; mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
SERVE_LOG="$LOG_DIR/serve.log"
: >"$SERVE_LOG"
command -v curl >/dev/null || (echo "curl missing" >&2; exit 2)
# build via helper and capture log
if ! "$TOOLS/build.sh" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/build.log"; then
  echo "build failed; see $LOG_DIR/build.log" >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOG_DIR/build.log" >&2 || true; exit 6
fi
[ -f "$WS/site/index.html" ] || (echo "site/index.html missing" >&2; exit 6)
# start server in its own process group so we can reliably kill it
nohup "$TOOLS/start.sh" >"$SERVE_LOG" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!
# give a moment for process group to settle
sleep 0.5
# determine PGID; if setsid used or exec'd, PGID should equal SERVER_PID
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo "")
TIMEOUT=${VALIDATION_TIMEOUT:-30}
elapsed=0
while [ $elapsed -lt $TIMEOUT ]; do
  if curl -sS --fail http://127.0.0.1:8000/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
  elapsed=$((elapsed+1))
done
if [ $elapsed -ge $TIMEOUT ]; then
  echo "server did not respond within ${TIMEOUT}s" >&2
  tail -n 400 "$SERVE_LOG" >&2 || true
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then
    kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    sleep 1
    kill -KILL -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  else
    kill "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  exit 7
fi
echo "Validation success: site built at $WS/site and mkdocs serve responded. PID=${SERVER_PID} PGID=${PGID}"
# stop server cleanly
if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then
  kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  sleep 1
  kill -KILL -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  kill "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  sleep 1
  kill -9 "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
